status: Literature option only; no geometry, native self-field solve or droplet result
concept: Inject current through feedstock/central electrode and return through the nozzle; nonuniform current interacts with its own magnetic field (electrovortex flow), potentially avoiding an actuator coil/permanent magnets.

primary_sources.title: Transient behaviour of electrovortex flow in a cylindrical container
primary_sources.supported_scope: Constant-current GaInSn experiment and simulation use a tapered electrode; self-field drives an electrovortex jet, and a weak axial background field changes its transient motion. This is confined bulk flow, not solder drop-on-demand at nozzle scale.

primary_sources.title: Experimental Study of the Velocity of the Electrovortex Flow of In-Ga-Sn in Hemispherical Geometry
primary_sources.access: Publisher-indexed abstract/results read; full open returned429.
primary_sources.supported_scope: Reported100–450A InGaSn velocity measurements establish the mechanism in their apparatus. Their500A contact-separation observation is not a transferable current limit for a micro-nozzle.

main_design_obstacle: Bare immersed feedstock permits current to leave along its length. It does not guarantee that terminal current reaches a small tip. An insulating sleeve or isolated electrode region may be required, reducing the proposed simplicity.
simulation_scope: Current research electrode client deliberately omits applied-current self-field. Running it with no applied magnetic field cannot test this option. A finite wire/current-return geometry and a validated self-field calculation are required first. Existing static self-field postprocessing is diagnostic only.
constraints: Do not substitute the axial-wire magnetic-pressure scale for actual nozzle pressure or a jetting threshold.
Current-return path, insulation, wire melting, interface resistance, thermal localization and interruption of wet contact matter.
Prefer current single-coil and external-contact evidence over presenting this untested alternative as a leading design.
